title: Rework console IO throttler and cache finesse
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Console backend has sporadic 95th/99th tail latency spikes during high-concurrency dashboard loads. Investigation points to the IO multiplexer (request throttler) and a coarse-grained in-memory cache that causes amplification under bursty traffic and synchronous GraphQL resolver fan-out. This ticket reworks the throttler path, adds a fine-grained shard-aware short-TTL segment cache, and upgrades key dependencies to remove blocking behavior in the request pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: 95th latency for aggregated dashboard endpoint reduced by >= 35% under the synthetic workload in staging
No increase in error rate (5xx) in canary rollout; circuit breaker triggers preserved
Merged PRs for throttler refactor and cache sharding; runtime flags to toggle new behavior
Dependency upgrade (graphql-js and node) completed and verified by integration tests
CI flamegraphs show reduced GC pauses attributable to cache refactor
technical_notes: Replace single global concurrentRequestLimiter with per-route multiplexers keyed by tenant+route to avoid head-of-line blocking
Introduce lightweight cache sharding using consistent hashing on request signature to reduce lock contention; each shard uses an LRU with 1000 entries and a 10s default TTL for hot prefixes
Move GraphQL resolver orchestration to async/continuation-style execution to avoid synchronous fan-out in the API gateway; use streaming partials where possible
Add observability: per-shard hit/miss/tombstone counters, multiplex queue length, and per-tenant tail-latency histogram exported to metrics pipeline
Upgrade graphql-js from 16.6 -> 17.1 and Node from 18.14 -> 20.8; audit transitive deps for native bindings causing blocking syscalls
